observedFacts.coverage: real AWS-LC TLS 1.2/1.3, trust, pins, hostname verification, mTLS, SNI, ALPN, resumption, external signer, lifecycle, fuzz mutations and corrected cleanup races

scopeConclusions.conclusion: The public client handshake installs explicit trust, keeps SNI separate from DNS/IP reference identity, rejects zoned IP references, enables peer verification and uses SAN-only matching without Common Name fallback. Pin verification still applies reference-identity verification. Native SAN output is two-pass and bounded.

PKCS#8 and SPKI inputs are bounded, exact-DER validated and copied into inaccessible owners; certificate/key matching occurs before use. Explicit close and finalization zero exportable private-key and session material. External signer and raw-RSA decryptor callbacks are bounded, execute outside the native callback, receive the handshake OperationContext and fail closed; returned decrypt blocks are length-checked and zeroed. The public built contexts do not expose their adopted decryptor.

Only TLS 1.2 and 1.3 are admitted. The public API exposes no cipher string, renegotiation, compression or 0-RTT enablement. Production uses the pinned AWS-LC defaults, disables early data for serialized sessions and partitions resumption by reference identity, ALPN, trust source, client identity, provider identity, security policy and checked context generation. Handshake, record, close-notify, truncation and no-progress terminals are typed and bounded.

The TLS, resolver and HTTP-files ABIs use explicit capacities and out lengths, reject invalid domains before allocation, validate native-returned counts in Cangjie and release pinned array views in finally blocks. Native partial failures close or cleanse owned resources. Resolver workers/jobs are bounded and reference-counted across late native completion. HTTP file access is descriptor-relative, no-follow, bounded and terminally cleaned.

Linux system trust selects an explicit bounded CA bundle or hashed directory and does not call provider-default trust lookup. The qualified artifact is Linux x86_64 glibc only. Its dynamic dependency set contains no libssl or libcrypto, and production TLS is the pinned static AWS-LC archive.

Production provider capabilities omit key logging; the release checks reject test-only keylog capability and system OpenSSL loader strings. Native pending keys, sessions, ticket keys, decrypt blocks and keylog buffers are cleansed on terminal paths. Evidence scanning found no PEM private keys or credential-header literals; keylog-label matches were synthetic source excerpts without emitted key bytes.

The native source pins, current source-input digests, rebuilt archive digests and installed artifact manifest agree for the reviewed qualification. A current upstream advisory screen found no listed AWS-LC advisory affecting upstream 5.5.0, but this is not an exhaustive third-party audit. The separate evidence-identity audit remains BLOCKED and prevents this slice from certifying the release packet as a whole.

gaps.title: Candidate evidence identity audit is blocked
gaps.reproduction: Read docs/evidence/M8-007/evidence-identity-audit.json and inspect status, results.candidate_mismatch_count and disposition.completion_prerequisites.
gaps.evidence: The current report says BLOCKED, records 133 candidate mismatches, and says 111 mismatches match current candidate bytes. This is an evidence-integrity gate, not a TLS source vulnerability.
gaps.requiredAction: Resolve the authorized replacement-candidate evidence identity and rerun the candidate-bound acceptance set; do not relabel historical outputs.

gaps.title: Formal soak and production signature remain outside this review
gaps.reproduction: Compare this review scope with docs/evidence/M8-007/security-scope.md final-gate exclusions and the authorization state supplied for this review.
gaps.evidence: The required 86,400-second soak and production signature have not completed. Older PASS-looking verification files are not accepted as current completion proof by this source review.
gaps.requiredAction: Complete and independently verify those final gates against the selected replacement candidate under separate authorization.

gaps.title: This process did not rerun a heavy native build, sanitizer campaign or exhaustive C ABI fuzz campaign
gaps.reproduction: Review the command list in this sidecar.
gaps.evidence: This process recomputed 29 native and 10 corrected-runtime source bindings, reviewed current code and existing raw execution evidence, and ran 53 targeted Python tests. The parser campaign is finite and does not claim exhaustive native ABI coverage.
gaps.requiredAction: Treat native-rebuild, TLS lifecycle and fuzz reports as bounded evidence; use an isolated scratch build and sanitizer/C ABI campaign if stronger assurance is required.

gaps.title: Internal native handles rely on trusted in-process callers
gaps.reproduction: Inspect the native handle lookup functions in native/tls/aws_lc/wirestack_tls_provider.c and corresponding resolver/filesystem bridges.
gaps.evidence: Handles are private pointer-valued ABI tokens guarded by magic values after dereference. Public Cangjie wrappers serialize ownership and zero handles before destroy; arbitrary forged or use-after-destroy calls by hostile in-process native code are outside the stated remote-peer threat model and were not certified.
gaps.requiredAction: Do not expose the internal native ABI to untrusted extensions. Add generation-indexed handle indirection before broadening that trust boundary.

gaps.title: System trust mutation is a trusted-local-input boundary
gaps.reproduction: Inspect src/internal/platform/linux/package.cj and src/internal/tls_engine/package.cj trust discovery and engine configuration.
gaps.evidence: The adapter hashes and then supplies explicit CA filesystem paths. Concurrent local mutation between discovery and provider load was not tested or certified; repository and system-trust administrators are trusted local actors in the declared threat model.
gaps.requiredAction: Preserve that trust assumption or snapshot/open the selected trust source atomically before admitting hostile local mutation into scope.

independenceAndConflicts.sharedModelConflict: Other process-isolated review slices may use the same model family or organizational toolchain; no model-diversity or external-human-independence claim is made.
independenceAndConflicts.sharedToolchainConflict: The review used repository digest helpers and qualification artifacts produced by the same project toolchain, with independent source reading and digest recomputation but without a separately implemented build system.

conclusion.summary: Current TLS, certificate identity, private-key, native-boundary and Linux-provider source was independently reviewed. No actionable vulnerability was found in this slice, and targeted controls passed. The blocked evidence-identity audit plus incomplete final soak and production-signature gates prevent a release-readiness or production-approval claim.
